::: {.petra-diagram .median-diagram}

**The median is the middle of the sorted values.** Arrange the data from smallest to largest first.

```{=html}
<div class="median-example">
<p class="example-label"><strong>Odd number of values: choose the middle value.</strong></p>
<ol class="median-values" style="--value-count:7" aria-label="Seven sorted values; the fourth value, 7, is the median">
<li>2</li><li>4</li><li>5</li><li class="middle-value">7</li><li>9</li><li>10</li><li>12</li>
</ol>
<p class="example-result">Median = <strong>7</strong></p>
</div>
<div class="median-example">
<p class="example-label"><strong>Even number of values: average the two middle values.</strong></p>
<ol class="median-values" style="--value-count:8" aria-label="Eight sorted values; the two middle values are 7 and 9">
<li>2</li><li>4</li><li>5</li><li class="middle-value">7</li><li class="middle-value">9</li><li>10</li><li>12</li><li>14</li>
</ol>
<p class="example-result">Median = (7 + 9) &divide; 2 = <strong>8</strong></p>
</div>
```

::: {.stat-formulas}

For sorted values $x_{(1)},\ldots,x_{(n)}$:

- **Odd $n$:** median $=x_{((n+1)/2)}$.
- **Even $n$:** median $=\bigl(x_{(n/2)}+x_{(n/2+1)}\bigr)/2$.

:::

**Why use it?** The median is less affected by extreme values than the mean.

:::
